description: We are a team of six enthusiastic engineering students interested in software development, Data Science, and space exploration. We have basic knowledge of Java, Python, HTML, and web development. We aim to develop an Astronaut Health Monitoring Application. We welcome passionate team members skilled in Python, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, AI/ML, UI/UX design, and data analysis. Let's collaborate, learn, and build something innovative!
summary:
Project Name
ASTRA CARE – An Interactive Virtual Model for Astronaut Health Monitoring
High-Level Project Summary
ASTRA CARE is a project developed to make astronaut health monitoring easier and more understandable. We created an interactive 3D model of an astronaut wearing a spacesuit. Users can rotate the model in 360 degrees, zoom in and explore nine different body regions.
By selecting different body parts, users can view available health information such as heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, ECG and EEG. The system also displays historical radiation exposure trends.
The main idea behind our project is to bring different astronaut health records and radiation information together in one place and present them in a visual and interactive way.
Why Is It Important?
During space missions, monitoring astronaut health and radiation exposure is very important. Instead of looking at different readings separately, our project allows users to explore the information through a 3D astronaut model.
It makes health information easier to view and understand. In the future, we hope to improve the project by connecting real-time wearable sensors and adding AI-based health risk alerts.
details:
1. What exactly does it do?

ASTRA CARE is a project that helps users explore astronaut health information through an interactive 3D model. It shows a full-body astronaut wearing a spacesuit. Users can rotate the model in 360 degrees, zoom in and explore nine different body regions.

When a user selects a body region, the application displays the available health records, such as heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, ECG and EEG. It also provides graphs to explore historical radiation exposure.

2. How does it work?

Users can interact with the 3D astronaut model directly through the application. They can select different body regions to view the related health information.

The frontend handles the 3D model and displays the health records through charts and visualizations. The Python FastAPI backend handles the data and sends the required information to the frontend.

3. What are its benefits?

  • Users can explore astronaut health information through a 3D model.
  • Different health records can be viewed in one place.
  • Historical radiation exposure can be understood through graphs.
  • The interactive model makes the monitoring system easier to explore.

4. What do we hope to achieve?

Through this project, we want to make astronaut health monitoring more interactive and easier to understand. In the future, we plan to connect wearable sensors to collect real-time health data and add AI-based alerts to identify unusual changes in health readings.

5. Tools and Technologies Used

  • React.js: Used to develop the frontend of the application.
  • Three.js: Used to create and interact with the 3D astronaut model.
  • Python FastAPI: Used for backend development and data processing.
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript: Used for web interface development, where applicable.

The current version works with historical and demonstration data. Real-time wearable sensor integration is planned for future development.
